No competing monitor-default rule is introduced here.
With I/O expanded, the documented Monitor reset command restores Off for audio and Auto for MIDI. This is a reset-context statement, not a universal new-track/custom-default/armed-track default.

In/Auto monitoring documents an enabled-by-default option to keep monitoring latency in recorded material, with manual switching through those Monitor controls. This establishes an option and context, not a timestamp correction formula or global constructor default.

Options exposes Delay Compensation, documented on by default for built-in devices and plug-ins including returns. The synchronization goal supplies no measured alignment, device-reporting contract or scheduling algorithm.

Reduced Latency When Monitoring is available with Delay Compensation on and changes compensation for input-monitored tracks while other compensated paths can remain different. Lowest-latency/in-sync language is an uncalibrated goal, not a zero-latency or alignment oracle.
Track Delay offers sample/ms units and is unavailable with Delay Compensation off. It is distinct from automatic compensation and device-owned Hardware Latency controls.

No latency arithmetic, graph maximum/difference calculation, driver/buffer/device-reporting law, clock phase/jitter, compensation accuracy, zero-latency deadline, CPU bound or calibration tolerance is established. Tempo-synced effects after delay and large-delay sluggishness are documented caveats only.

### REQ-RECORDING-COMPING-002 — input monitoring

**D12, R17 §17.1.** Auto passes input when armed and inhibits monitoring while
clips play. In continuously passes input and suppresses clip output regardless
of arm. Off disables monitoring; it permits recording with external monitoring.
A Monitor choice applies to all selected tracks. This clause specifies a
selection/gating result, not a latency or signal-processing tolerance.
**U:** factory/new-track defaults: R19 §19.2 calls monitoring of armed tracks
the default, while R17 §17.1 describes reset defaults of Off for audio and Auto
for MIDI. Preserve the contextual distinction; do not impose one global default.
